clusters.name: Counterfactual explanation: an edited input that would change the decision
clusters.description: An alternative input that would lead the model to a different decision, offered as the explanation (written by the model itself in 5 of the 10 papers) and judged by validity, minimality and closeness.

clusters.name: Counterfactual simulatability: an explanation that predicts behavior on other inputs
clusters.description: An explanation is good insofar as an observer who reads it (a human, an LLM judge or a simulator model) can predict the model's output on other, counterfactual inputs.

clusters.name: The counterfactual set: which inputs simulatability is tested on
clusters.description: Which inputs the simulatability test runs on: LLM-written follow-up questions, cue-removed inputs, rejection-sampled model edits, Gricean what-if variations, or nearby real dataset rows, and the pitfalls of each.

clusters.name: Counterfactual self-prediction: the model reports how it would behave under an edit
clusters.description: The model itself is the observer: it states whether or how an edit would change its own behavior, and the statement is scored against runs on the edited input. A counterfactual form of self-report.

clusters.name: Input intervention: the same input with one cue or factor changed
clusters.description: The same input with one cue, attribute, factor, evidence passage or conversation turn removed, inserted or replaced, all else fixed; the output difference is read as that element's causal influence.

clusters.name: From paired runs to a causal claim: flip labels, total effects and potential outcomes
clusters.description: How runs on the original and the variant become a claim that the edit caused the outcome: a per-pair flip label, a thresholded resampled rate, a population total effect, or bounds on potential outcomes.

clusters.name: Valid counterfactuals: isolation, quality and controls
clusters.description: What a variant must satisfy before an output change can be attributed to the intended edit: isolation of one factor, coherence, being on-policy, opposing the baseline, executability, controls, and for parameter edits, efficacy and specificity.

clusters.name: The counterfactual test of explanations: does the explanation mention the edit?
clusters.description: An input edit that flips the prediction is used to judge the explanation, which is unfaithful if it does not mention the edit (Atanasova et al. 2023), or a correlation between mentions and graded influence (Siegel et al. 2024).

clusters.name: Intervention on the reasoning: an edited, truncated or resampled chain of thought
clusters.description: An edited, truncated, substituted, injected or resampled chain of thought (or other model-produced intermediate) with the input fixed; the answer's response measures dependence on the reasoning.

clusters.name: Counterfactual training pairs
clusters.description: A counterfactual rationale, context or prediction pair used as training data or reward signal, training either sensitivity to the reasoning or invariance to a cue or pressure.

clusters.name: Counterfactual internal states and parameters
clusters.description: An alternative value of something inside the model (attention weights, patched activations, an edited knowledge triple, a permuted span's Jacobian, or unlearned parameters), with any input edit serving only as a donor.

clusters.name: Counterfactual baselines for scheming, obfuscation and dishonesty
clusters.description: A comparison condition that shows a behavior to be strategic, hidden or dishonest when no single trajectory can: reversed incentives for sandbagging, self versus successor for sabotage, attribute swaps for steganographic reliance, a no-defect scenario for obfuscated denial, a neutral variant for knowledge in honesty scoring.
